description: CAPS-approved method: morphological identification by conidiophore structure and size and conidial shape and size. Isozyme comparison has also been used. At the time of writing there was no species-specific PCR (only tools for related species, such as a *P. sorghi* SCAR and a *P. sacchari* DNA probe).
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

description: Since other endemic downy mildews (*P. maydis*, *P. spontanea*) produce similar symptoms, field symptoms alone cannot give accurate identification. Molecular identification is needed for confirmation.
source_name: USDA CAPS datasheet *P. philippinensis* Version 2 (2021-09-29) (CAPS-Pp-2021)

description: In a 62-ortholog phylogeny, the *P. philippinensis* lectotype (BPI 187314) belongs to subgroup B2 and falls in a different clade from the *P. sacchari* lectotype. Therefore the two species are kept separate. The conspecific view based on morphology, host range and isozymes was not adopted. Host range is of little diagnostic use.
short_quote: "both taxa were upheld as distinct species"
source_name: Groben G. et al. 2026, Fungal Syst. Evol. 17:221–232 (CC BY 4.0) (Groben2026)
location_in_source: Discussion 'P. philippinensis and P. sacchari'; Taxonomy

description: Maize downy mildews are caused by up to 10 species in the genera *Peronosclerospora*, *Sclerophthora* and *Sclerospora*. Other endemic downy mildews (e.g., *P. sorghi*) and physiological disorders (fertility, weather) also produce similar symptoms. MSV infection can mask downy mildew symptoms.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)
location_in_source: p.4 Known Vectors; p.6 Easily Confused Pests

description: Other downy mildews in the same table: sugarcane downy mildew (*S. sacchari*) has yellow to white streaks at the base of leaves 3–6 and increased ear number; sorghum downy mildew has pale green to cream parallel streaks and a fan of small leaves at the plant top; crazy top has chlorotic streaks weaker than Philippine downy mildew and phyllody of the tassel. Downy mildews differ only in detailed symptoms, so **species cannot be accurately identified from field symptoms alone**.
source_name: Singh J., "Relative disease reaction of maize varieties to downy mildews over varied environments (IDMN 1969–1973)", Tropical Agriculture Research Series No. 8, pp.129–152 (JIRCAS publication; **publication year unconfirmed in the original**) (Singh-TARS8)

description: Korean source: Unconfirmed. Korea is not in the EPPO distribution (India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand). Only Identity and distribution of the EPPO web datasheet could be viewed.
source_name: EPPO-SCPHRZ

description: The latest name is "*Sclerophthora zeae* (formerly *S. rayssiae* var. *zeae*)", described as a US Select Agent. The publication establishing this combination is Unconfirmed.
source_name: Groben G. et al. 2026, Fungal Syst. Evol. 17:221–232 (CC BY 4.0) (Groben2026)

description: Lesions form **only on leaves**. At first they are narrow chlorotic or yellow streaks like other downy mildews but only **3–7 mm** wide. Borders are distinct and delimited by veins. In some genotypes they later turn red to purple.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: Narrow chlorotic or yellow streaks of variable length, bounded by veins. They later become necrotic and take on a **brown, burnt appearance**.
source_name: Singh J., "Relative disease reaction of maize varieties to downy mildews over varied environments (IDMN 1969–1973)", Tropical Agriculture Research Series No. 8, pp.129–152 (JIRCAS publication; **publication year unconfirmed in the original**) (Singh-TARS8)

description: As lesions spread laterally they become severe striping and blotching. They are noticeable first and most severe on lower leaves and look pale brown and burnt. Severely affected leaves may drop early.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: Blotching before flowering suppresses grain development, giving small seed, and plants may die early. If more than 3/4 of the leaf is infected before flowering, total loss is possible, and ear formation is completely suppressed or greatly weakened.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: Unlike other downy mildews, **floral or vegetative organs are not malformed and leaves do not shred**. It appears not to infect systemically.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: Spores form on both lesion surfaces, appearing downy or woolly. When lesions become necrotic, sporangia disappear.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: Check for down on both leaf surfaces on **cool, humid mornings**. The down usually disappears by late afternoon. Infected leaves remain intact.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: Oospores and oogonia are scattered abundantly in the mesophyll of necrotic tissue or below stomata. They are not in the vascular bundles.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: Young plants are most susceptible, and susceptibility declines with age. Zinc deficiency predisposes plants to infection. Soil temperatures of 28–32 °C are favorable. Under humid conditions at 22–25 °C sporangia form in 3 hours and a second generation appears after 9 hours. 12 hours of leaf wetness is required.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: An obligate biotroph. Sporangiophores are short and determinate, emerging from substomatal cavities. Sporangia are hyaline, ovoid to nearly cylindrical, operculate, **18.5–26 × 29–66.5 µm**, borne in groups of 2–6 with a distinct peduncle and smooth walls. Each contains 4–8 zoospores. Encysted zoospores are globose, 7.5–11 µm.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: Oogonia are 33–44.5 µm in diameter, subglobose, thin-walled, hyaline to pale straw-colored. Oospores are **29.5–37 µm**, globose to subglobose, with a smooth, glossy wall 4 µm thick fused to the oogonial wall. Contents are hyaline with a distinct oil globule. More are formed at high temperatures above 28 °C.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: Table 1: *S. rayssiae* var. *zeae* has short, hypha-like, determinate sporangiophores. Sporangia are 18.5–26 × 29–66.5 µm and **germinate by zoospores**. Oospores are brown, globose, 29.5–37 µm. In contrast, conidiophores of the four *Peronosclerospora* species are long (150–550 µm) and dichotomously branched, and conidia **germinate by a germ tube**. Sporangia of *S. macrospora* (crazy top) are lemon-shaped, 30–60 × 60–100 µm, and oospores are mainly in vascular bundles.
source_name: USDA CAPS Small Grains manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (Table 1, citing White 1999) (CAPS-Pp-SG)

description: The CAPS-approved method is morphological identification. "No serological or molecular diagnostic methods are known" (at the time of writing). NPDN has produced a diagnostic standard operating procedure (SOP).
short_quote: "no known serological or molecular diagnostic methods"
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: *Sclerophthora* is likely a species complex, or many misidentifications occurred in the past through morphological identification. This study first clearly separated *Sclerophthora* and *Peronosclerospora* by molecular means.
source_name: Groben G. et al. 2026, Fungal Syst. Evol. 17:221–232 (CC BY 4.0) (Groben2026)

description: Crazy top (*S. macrospora*): phyllody, with the tassel turning into a leafy mass, and excessive tillering. Sorghum downy mildew (*P. sorghi*): chlorosis, frequent stunting, white streaks, narrow upright leaves and phyllody of the tassel. **None** of these symptoms is observed with brown stripe downy mildew. Var. *rayssiae* (barley downy mildew) is very similar but differs in host range.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: Physiological disorders (fertility, weather and so on) and other endemic downy mildews can also produce similar symptoms.
source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

description: Early MLN symptoms: **mosaic and mottling**.
source_name: CIMMYT, "Disease Symptoms of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN)" flyer (CIMMYT-Flyer)

description: **Necrosis starting at the leaf margins** appears together with mottling.
source_name: CIMMYT, "Disease Symptoms of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN)" flyer (CIMMYT-Flyer)

description: **'Dead heart'** symptom (death of the growing point and young leaves).
source_name: CIMMYT, "Disease Symptoms of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN)" flyer (CIMMYT-Flyer)

description: Husks dry early, and grain filling is poor or there is no grain set.
source_name: CIMMYT, "Disease Symptoms of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN)" flyer (CIMMYT-Flyer)

description: Three-column layout of the flyer: SCMV symptoms = 'mild mosaic and mottling'; MCMV symptoms = 'shortened internodes, severe chlorotic mottling'. Whether the second-row 'severe chlorosis and leaf necrosis' belongs to the MCMV or the MLN column is unclear from the layout (**interpret with caution**).
source_name: CIMMYT, "Disease Symptoms of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN)" flyer (CIMMYT-Flyer)

description: Common MLN symptoms: chlorotic spots intensify, growth is suppressed and plants yellow. Long yellow streaks wider than MSV streaks form. Leaves yellow and dry **from the outer margin toward the midrib**, and whole plants usually dry and die **from the top down**. Dead plants are **scattered** among healthy-looking plants.
short_quote: "higher intensity of chlorotic spots, stunted growth and yellowing"
source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

description: With late infection tassels fail to emerge and ears are poor: small and malformed, with few kernels or empty.
source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

description: Newly emerging leaves show marginal necrosis. Upper internodes shorten, and young leaves develop streaks, mottling, mosaic and narrow stripes. Plants are shorter, and distinct pale green-yellow mottling persists to the end of the season. Single infections can recover from mosaic, but in MLN the mottling persists.
source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

description: Plants infected with MCMV alone show **pale green mottling** alternating light and dark green.
source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

description: SCMV alone: mosaic with normal-green 'islands' embedded in a pale green or chlorotic background. It is most distinct on fast-growing young leaves and fades as leaves age.
source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

category: Symptoms - whole plant (MCMV alone vs MLN)
description: MCMV infection symptoms: chlorotic mottling, mosaic, chlorotic and necrotic streaks, leaf necrosis, stunting, poor ear development, malformed ears and early death. Severity depends on genotype, age at infection, environment, isolate and co-occurring viruses. MLN mixed infections are usually more severe than single infections, and early infection causes systemic necrosis, severe stunting, death and large yield losses.
source_name: CDFA California Pest Rating Proposal: Maize chlorotic mottle virus (comment period 2026-07-16 to 08-30) (CDFA-MCMV)

description: MCMV inoculation alone: **mild chlorotic mottling** on new leaves after 10 days (agro-inoculation) or 6 days (sap inoculation), with mild symptoms. MCMV+SCMV co-infection: **severe systemic necrosis** (CLND) of leaves and stems (figure 15 days after inoculation).
source_name: Wang Q. et al. 2017, Scientific Reports 7:39960 (PMC5216416) (Wang2017)

description: 1–9 scale for MCMV resistance evaluation: 6 = strong chlorotic mottling and marginal necrosis over the whole plant; 8 = excessive chlorotic mottling, leaf necrosis, dead heart, sometimes early death; 9 = necrosis of the whole plant, sometimes death. The final score is taken 40 days after the first inoculation.
growth_stage: Up to about 40 days after inoculation
source_name: Prasanna B.M. et al. 2020, Virus Research 282:197943 (PMC7221342) (Prasanna2020)

description: MCMV or SCMV alone usually cause milder symptoms, and together they rapidly act synergistically. Plants are susceptible at **all growth stages** from seedling to maturity.
source_name: CIMMYT MLN portal, Causes & Symptoms (CIMMYT-Causes)

description: Some plants may carry the viruses without symptoms (especially tolerant varieties).
source_name: Prasanna B.M. et al. 2020, Virus Research 282:197943 (PMC7221342) (Prasanna2020)

description: Drought, poor soil and poor crop management make MLN more severe.
source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

description: The first detection in Kenya was in September 2011 (southern Rift Valley). Yield losses in affected counties in 2012–13 were 23–100%.
source_name: Prasanna B.M. et al. 2020, Virus Research 282:197943 (PMC7221342) (Prasanna2020)

description: Non-enveloped, monopartite **spherical** particles with a T=3 icosahedral capsid of 180 protein subunits, about **30 nm** in diameter. The genome is 4,436 nt.
source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

description: MCMV has isometric particles about 30 nm in diameter.
source_name: Wang Q. et al. 2017, Scientific Reports 7:39960 (PMC5216416) (Wang2017)

description: (+)ssRNA, isometric particles. Tombusviridae, Machlomovirus, species name *Machlomovirus zeae*.
source_name: CDFA California Pest Rating Proposal: Maize chlorotic mottle virus (comment period 2026-07-16 to 08-30) (CDFA-MCMV)

description: Flexuous filamentous particles **708 nm** long. Pinwheel and scroll-type inclusion bodies are characteristic. Genome length is given inconsistently within the document as 9,610 nt and 5–12 kb.
source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

description: Flexuous filamentous particles and pinwheel-shaped inclusion bodies were observed only in co-infected cells. Length is not described.
source_name: Wang Q. et al. 2017, Scientific Reports 7:39960 (PMC5216416) (Wang2017)

description: MCMV is transmitted by thrips and beetles: the maize thrips *Frankliniella williamsi*, the corn flea beetle *C. pulicaria*, *Diabrotica undecimpunctata*, *D. longicornis* and *D. virgifera*, *Systena frontalis* and *Oulema melanopa*. Potyviruses are transmitted mainly by aphids (*Aphis gossypii*, *Myzus persicae*). Vector morphology is not described.
source_name: CIMMYT MLN portal, Causes & Symptoms (CIMMYT-Causes)

description: SCMV is transmitted non-persistently by aphids, the most efficient species being *Rhopalosiphum maidis*, *R. padi* and *Schizaphis graminum*. For MCMV it says *F. williamsi* is the most common vector in Africa. The text calls it 'the only reported arthropod vector' while Table 2 also lists beetles, a contradiction within the document.
source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

description: Field symptoms cannot identify the causal viruses. DAS-ELISA (commercial MCMV and SCMV kits), RT-PCR (amplicons MCMV 550 bp, SCMV 900 bp), NGS, Northern blot and TaqMan probes are used.
source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

description: The MCMV ImmunoStrip is a fast, inexpensive field test widely used in East African seed production fields (6 young leaves per ha sampled in an X pattern and pooled). ELISA is used for MCMV seed testing. RT-PCR is more sensitive than ELISA. Because SCMV is highly diverse, serological results may be inconsistent.
source_name: Prasanna B.M. et al. 2020, Virus Research 282:197943 (PMC7221342) (Prasanna2020)

description: The symptom description in Wangai et al. 2012 (Plant Dis. 96:1582, first report from Kenya) (chlorotic mottling at the base of young whorl leaves, necrosis from margin to midrib, dead heart) is **Unconfirmed because the original was not viewed**. The earlier notes also had only a search summary.
source_name: Wangai et al. 2012, Plant Disease 96:1582 (full text could not be opened)
